description: Hi! 🚀 I'm a third-year CSE-AIML student passionate about AI, machine learning, Python, web development, and space exploration. I love building innovative solutions to real-world problems using technology and NASA's open data. I'm looking for collaborative teammates skilled in AI/ML, coding, data analysis, Earth science, UI/UX design, and space exploration. Let's combine our skills, think creatively, and build an impactful solution together! 🌍✨
summary:
FLAMEWISE is an open-science microgravity combustion intelligence and research platform that transforms decades of authentic NASA flight data into actionable insights for spacecraft fire safety. By synthesizing 24 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigations, 2,783 flight experiment runs, and 22,312 physical measurements, FLAMEWISE addresses the challenge of making complex, siloed space science intuitive, verifiable, and operationally useful.

The platform integrates an interactive real-time 3D combustion physics simulator, multi-variable Plotly scientific analytics, an Artemis exploration atmosphere flammability calculator, and an evidence-grounded AI research assistant built on a strict zero-hallucination protocol.

FLAMEWISE is vital for the future of human space exploration. Upcoming Artemis Lunar Gateway and Mars transit missions will operate in reduced-pressure, elevated-oxygen cabin environments (8.2 psia at 34% O₂)—a unique regime where terrestrial 1g fire standards fail to predict flame spread. By bridging historical microgravity experiments with predictive models, FLAMEWISE empowers researchers, flight engineers, and safety boards to design safer habitats for deep-space exploration.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

FLAMEWISE is a full-stack scientific research platform designed to unlock, analyze, and visualize NASA microgravity combustion flight data. In zero gravity, buoyancy-driven natural convection is eliminated (Grashof number Gr → 0), causing flames to burn as stationary, spherical diffusion shells governed purely by molecular transport and radiative cooling.

FLAMEWISE translates this complex fluid dynamics through five interconnected capabilities:

• Real-Time 3D Combustion Simulator: An in-browser WebGL physics sandbox built with Three.js that dynamically contrasts Earth’s buoyant teardrop flame against microgravity’s spherical diffusion flame, recalculating Grashof (Gr) and Péclet (Pe) numbers live as gravity, oxygen concentration, and fuels change.

• NASA Flight Data Explorer: Fast, multi-parameter filtering across 24 verified NASA combustion campaigns (ACME, BASS, BASS-II, FLEX, SAFFIRE, SPICE), 2,783 flight runs, and 22,312 physical measurements.

• Plotly Scientific Analytics: Multi-variable scatter, bubble, and composition charts mapping chamber pressure, airflow velocity, oxygen concentration, and flame temperature with full zoom, hover inspection, and publication-ready export.

• Artemis Flammability Calculator: An aerospace safety tool modeling Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI) shifts and flame spread rates across spacecraft materials (PMMA, Nomex, Silicone, SIBAL) under Artemis Exploration Atmospheres (8.2 psia at 34% O₂).

• Evidence-Grounded AI Research Assistant: A scientific synthesis engine that delivers structured 5-part explanations grounded strictly in NASA database records, complete with verified NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS) and PSI citations with direct PDF download links.

2. What benefits does it have?

• Unlocks Siloed NASA Research: Converts scattered, heterogeneous spreadsheets and technical reports into a high-speed, queryable relational database.

• Rapid Scientific Comparison: Enables combustion scientists to perform side-by-side evaluations of opposed vs. concurrent airflows, extinction limits, and temperature differentials in seconds rather than weeks.

• Zero-Hallucination AI Integrity: Unlike generic LLMs that invent scientific numbers, our AI Assistant queries authentic database tables and transparently discloses when experimental data is absent.

• Interactive Education: Allows educators and students worldwide to interact with zero-gravity combustion physics that cannot be demonstrated in normal Earth-bound classrooms.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Fire is one of the most fatal threats aboard crewed space missions. NASA's upcoming Artemis Lunar Gateway and Mars transit habitats plan to use low-pressure, high-oxygen cabin atmospheres (8.2 psia at 34% O₂) to eliminate astronaut pre-breathe times prior to spacewalks. Terrestrial flammability qualification tests (NASA-STD-6001B) performed in normal air (14.7 psia at 21% O₂) fail to capture the prolonged residence times and lower radiative extinction boundaries found in microgravity.

FLAMEWISE directly impacts mission safety by providing mission architects, materials scientists, and environmental control life-support system (ECLSS) engineers with the empirical foundation needed to select fire-resistant materials and design smarter fire suppression systems for lunar and deep-space missions.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

• Languages: JavaScript (ES6+), Python 3.10, SQL, HTML5, CSS3

• Frontend Framework: React 19, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide React

• 3D Simulation & Graphics: Three.js (WebGL rendering, procedural particle systems)

• Scientific Visualization: Plotly.js (Hardware-accelerated data visualization)

• Backend & API Microservice: Python FastAPI, Uvicorn ASGI server, Pydantic v2 data models

• Database & ETL Pipeline: Normalized SQLite relational database (PostgreSQL migration ready), SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM, Python data ingestion scripts

• Cloud Hosting & Deployment: Firebase Hosting (Google Cloud Global Edge CDN), Render Cloud Microservice

5. How is your project creative?

• Living Physics Sandbox: Instead of displaying static charts, FLAMEWISE lets users physically toggle gravity fields and manipulate oxygen fractions to see real-time 3D flame envelope transitions and fluid dynamics.

• Exploration Atmosphere Calculator: Translates fundamental combustion physics into a practical mission calculator tailored directly to NASA’s current Artemis Moon-to-Mars roadmap.

• Judges Fast-Track Tour: Includes a built-in interactive guided walkthrough modal and a keyboard-driven Command Palette (Ctrl+K) for streamlined discovery.

• Strict Epistemic Grounding: Combines generative synthesis with relational database matching to ensure every scientific claim cites authentic NASA Glenn Research Center flight telemetry.

6. What factors did your team consider?

• Scientific Validity: Ensured 100% data integrity with zero fabricated metrics, preserving SI and NASA engineering units (Kelvin, atmospheres, mg/s, psia, mole fractions).

• Architectural Scalability: Engineered a decoupled client-server architecture with sub-50ms API query times across 22,000+ data rows.

• User Experience: Developed an aerospace-grade dark scientific theme with balanced typographic hierarchy, responsive layout across desktop and mobile screens, and accessible contrast ratios.

• Operational Relevance: Aligned our analytical tools directly with real-world spacecraft fire safety challenges identified in NASA flight reports.
